status.label: Reproducible selection/ranking mismatch
status.detail: Frequency sorting starts at index zero while arrow-key selection can start in the middle.

next_action.label: Verify center-start frequency behavior
next_action.reason: The report supplies the exact two-setting combination; no reporter logs are needed.

judgment.rationale: This report concerns ranked items being far from the initial central selection, not frequency persistence or complete failure to sort. Available source contains both sides of that mismatch.
evidence: The body sets frequency sorting ON and start-from-left OFF, then trains several characters.
PowerAccent.Core/PowerAccent.cs GetCharacters sorts by descending usage into the left-to-right array.
The initial arrow selection uses the middle indices when StartSelectionFromTheLeft is false; Space instead starts at an edge.
Related issue 25217 describes incomplete sorting, while other cross-references concern restarting frequency counts; none establishes this center-selection report is handled.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce arrow versus Space activation and agree the centered ranking policy before implementing the bounded selection/ranking correction.

fix_assessment.rationale: A targeted Quick Accent ordering/selection change is applicable; no concrete owner or implementation covers this specific interaction.

proposed_fixes.title: Align frequency-ranked characters with center-start navigation
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The inspected frequency sort places the most-used character at index zero while center-start arrow navigation selects a middle index. The appropriate symmetric ordering and ties still need UX validation.
plan: Add a regression for frequency sorting enabled and start-from-left disabled, covering Left, Right and Space activation separately.

Define and implement a stable center-out permutation for frequency-ranked candidates when center-start arrow navigation is used, or an agreed selection rule that makes the top-ranked candidate immediately reachable.
Keep left-start and Space activation semantics unchanged unless explicitly approved; preserve usage counts, case conversion and character descriptions.
Test odd/even candidate counts, ties and empty/single-entry lists.
verification: Train a character and reopen with each activation key; verify the most-used item is nearest the intended initial selection.
Verify existing start-from-left and reverse/Shift navigation tests still pass.

confidence.rationale: The reported setting combination maps directly to the inspected array sort and middle-index selection; the final interaction policy and runtime behavior have not been independently validated.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent's frequency-sorted candidates stay at the left edge even when arrow-key navigation begins centrally, making common accents farther away.
known_information: PowerToys 0.79.0 and the exact setting combination are supplied.
The only comment is a similarity bot; there is no assignee or targeted linked implementation.
The source separates frequency sorting from initial navigation index selection.
inferences: This is an interaction between ordering and initial selection rather than proof that usage counting is broken.
issue_context.analysis: The old ownership claim was unsupported. The report is sufficient to reproduce locally and review a focused plan without asking for generic diagnostics.
initial_investigation: Read the entire report, bot comment and cross-reference timeline.
Read GetCharacters and the initial-selection branches in PowerAccent.cs.
Compared the linked frequency-sorting report's different symptom.

actions.label: Review centered frequency plan
actions.description: Approve a bounded UX/regression investigation, not an already-converged design.

prerequisites: Use a current build and a language/key with multiple accent candidates.
Enable Sort characters by usage frequency and disable Start selection from the left.
steps: Select one accent repeatedly to establish a leading usage rank.
Reopen the toolbar using Left and then Right activation; record the initial selection and leading accent location.
Enable start-from-left and repeat as a control.
reproduce.expected_result: Frequently used candidates are immediately reachable under the agreed selection policy without regressing edge-start controls.
